description: Package README: result summary, size/distance sensitivity, folder map, one-command reproduction, seeds and nulls, guardrails.

One-command reproduction: checks the input tables (or rebuilds them from the public files with --from-public), runs the three analysis scripts, compares outputs with the archived and reference files, and checks every analysis number quoted in the v3 paper and appendix, at its printed precision, plus the canonical sensitivity numbers (PASS/FAIL per check, total, report).

Rebuilds data/manga_dynpop_merged_thin_firstpass.csv and data/manga_dynpop_DA_target.csv from the three public MaNGA DynPop files (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.17518315 and 10.5281/zenodo.15742825), checking their Zenodo MD5s; --compare checks a rebuild against data/ (every column identical or within 2 ulps, same NaN pattern; on the reference platform 52 of 54 columns are bit-identical).
Refreshes this manifest (bytes and SHA-256 of every file; descriptions kept from file_manifest.csv); --check compares without writing and reports CRLF-only differences separately.
Tested Python package versions (Python 3.10.14); astropy and h5py are needed only by build_merged_table.py.
Ignores generated folders: reproduce_outputs/, regenerated/, data/rebuilt/, __pycache__/.
Main paper: Two Layers of Galaxy Aging in MaNGA DynPop: A Principle-Level Proof of Concept.
Supplementary appendix: detailed methodology, literature passes, control-variable specifications, limitation analyses, and sensitivity documentation.

Sources of the redistributed data: the two CC BY 4.0 Zenodo records (creators, versions), the public files used with their MD5s, and what the package changed (column subset, PlateIFU join, derived columns, sentinels set to NaN).

Joined working table (10,296 PlateIFU rows x 54 columns) from the public DynPop JAM v2, SP/SFH v2 and DynPop VII CVC catalogs (CC BY 4.0); the table recovered from the original analysis and read by every script. logRe is log10 of the MGE effective radius in arcsec.

plateifu, mangaid, DA (adopted angular-diameter distance, Mpc) and target (MaNGA subsample: 0 Primary, 1 Secondary, 2 color-enhanced) copied from SDSSDR17_MaNGA_JAM_v2.fits HDU 1; read by the size/distance sensitivity script.

Strict-control pipeline (portable version of the archived 2026-06-29 script; analysis code unchanged): reduced control model (one term per quantity), controlled dynamical-residual young/old quartile split, bootstrap and within-bin age-shuffle nulls, cross-validated age gain, Spearman check; writes all six CSVs in this folder plus a Markdown report.
Primary strict-control summary: young-vs-old controlled-residual scoreboard for the intrinsic, observed, and both-SPS control sets (7/8 bins each).
Controlled-residual scoreboard with bootstrap 95% intervals and shuffle-null distribution statistics for the three strict-control SPS sets.

Per-bin controlled dynamical residual table across the eight stellar-mass bins for each strict-control set; the sixth bin (index 5, median NSA log M = 10.66) is the only young < old bin in all three sets.
Controlled-model term table: standardized T50 coefficient, robust SE/t/p, model R2, cross-validated delta-R2 from age, and Spearman rho for each SPS control set.
Age (T50) coefficients on the raw dynamical-M/L outcome per 1 SD of T50, with robust SE, p-value, and model R2 for each control set.
Reduced-spec sensitivity grid (metallicity weighting x flattening term x SPS set): all 12 variants give 7/8 bins. The grid does not vary the size term or distance; see 03_size_distance_sensitivity/.
Handoff note documenting the strict-control specification choice, the main 7/8-bin result, age/CV/rank checks, the single non-decisive bin, and the main-text recommendation.
Clean-pipeline v0.6 working draft of the two-layer note (superseded by the final paper; retained as provenance).
v0.6 revision notes: abstract tightening, framework-language changes, and integration of the simulation/assembly-bias pass.
Unified diff from draft v0.5 to v0.6.

Simulation and assembly-bias literature pass: no exact mock-MaNGA/JAM/SPS controlled-residual comparator located; the residual is unbenchmarked against cosmological mocks, not proven anomalous relative to LambdaCDM.
Primary DML sledgehammer report: fixed-mass young/old DML split, 8/8 observed-SPS and 6/8 intrinsic-SPS bins, plus the secondary fDM checks.
DML sledgehammer scoreboard for the observed- and intrinsic-SPS definitions.
Per-bin DML results across the eight stellar-mass bins.
Figure: kitchen-table plot of young and old median DML across the eight mass bins for both SPS definitions.
Figure: overall mass-adjusted young/old DML comparison with bootstrap intervals.
Figure: per-bin young-minus-old DML differences.
M/L split and controlled-residual hardening report: numerator/denominator decomposition and the (kitchen-sink) controlled dynamical residual.
Raw M/L component split scoreboard: JAM dynamical logM/L, intrinsic SPS, and observed SPS log M*/L.
Kitchen-sink controlled dynamical-residual scoreboard (8/8 observed and both SPS, 6/8 intrinsic SPS; original specification, retained as supplementary sensitivity).
Per-bin M/L split and controlled-residual table across the eight mass bins.
Figure: M/L component split kitchen-table plot.
Figure: DML component decomposition showing the SPS denominator dominates the raw signal.
Figure: controlled dynamical M/L residuals, young vs old, after SPS/metallicity/structural controls.
Figure: overall mass-adjusted controlled-residual young/old comparison.
SHA256 checksums for the original v0.6 clean-pipeline bundle files, as released.

Secondary fDM checks (gNFW and NFW fDM within Re): bins with young > old, mean bin young-old difference, and count, magnitude and joint shuffle p (5,000 shuffles). Source of Table 1 fDM count p and magnitude p. Added from the 2026-06-26 sledgehammer outputs bundle; not part of the v0.6 bundle, so not in manifest_sha256.txt.

Re-implementation (2026-10; the v0.6 code was not preserved) of the raw DML split, M/L component split, secondary fDM checks, nearest-mass paired check, sample counts and T50 grid facts. Reproduces every v0.6 point estimate exactly; shuffle p and bootstrap intervals agree with v0.6 to Monte Carlo precision. Default null: exchangeable within-bin value permutation.

Reference run: scoreboard for the 7 outcomes (bins, mean bin and mass-adjusted young-old differences with bootstrap 95% CIs, young>old and old>young count/magnitude/joint shuffle p, sign-test reference p).
Reference run: per-bin young and old medians, differences and bootstrap 95% CIs for the 7 outcomes.
Reference run: nearest-mass paired check for DML intrinsic and observed SPS (881 and 913 young wins of 1,488 pairs, binomial and shuffle p).
Reference run: per-bin T50 facts for the young and old quartiles (medians, ranges, IQRs, counts at and above the 12.85 Gyr mode, tie groups at the quartile cuts).
Reference run: sample counts (10,296 joined entries of 10,160 MaNGA IDs; 6,065 with Qual >= 1; 5,952 in the sample, 5,875 distinct MaNGA IDs).
Reference run: archived v0.6 values next to the rerun values for every sledgehammer quantity, deterministic and Monte Carlo, with Monte Carlo SE for p-values.
Reference run: input SHA-256, seeds, null, sample counts, T50 grid summary and software versions.

Size/distance/subsample sensitivity of the controlled residual using the strict-control functions at 5,000 bootstraps and shuffles: published spec, size in kpc, + log distance, kpc + log distance, MaNGA Primary-only and Secondary-only samples, and the kitchen-sink controls; plus quartile distances, Secondary fractions and SPS attenuation terms per bin, the 12-variant grid by size treatment with the HC3 t of a linear T50 term, one-cube-per-MaNGA-ID point estimates (controlled residual in arcsec and kpc size), and the young/old split with tied T50 values broken at random (200 draws per row).
Reference run: one row per variant and SPS set (bins, mass-adjusted residual and CI, count/magnitude/joint p, standardized and per-Gyr T50 coefficients with HC3 t/p, CV Delta R^2, Spearman rho).
Reference run: per-bin controlled residuals for every variant and SPS set.

Reference run: per mass bin, median DA, Secondary-sample fraction and SPS attenuation term (sp_ML_obs_Re - sp_ML_int_Re) of the young and old quartiles (young lie 1.18 to 1.67 times farther away; 2.05 to 3.54 times more often Secondary; old quartile carries the larger attenuation term in the four lowest mass bins).

Reference run: the 12-variant reduced-spec grid under each size treatment (arcsec, kpc, arcsec + log distance, kpc + log distance): point estimates and the HC3 t and p of a linear T50 term (t from -12.7 to -4.2; largest p 2.8e-5).

Reference run: every Table 1 row, with the controlled residual for size in arcsec and in kpc, for the full sample and for one entry per MaNGA ID (bin counts unchanged; mass-adjusted differences move by at most 0.0019).

Reference run: the young/old quartile split with tied T50 values at the quartile cuts broken at random instead of by stellar mass, 200 draws per row (seed 20260629 + 9000), for the 12-variant grid under angular size, kpc size and angular size + log distance and for the Primary- and Secondary-only rows: bins and mass-adjusted difference under the stellar-mass rule, and the range, median and histogram of bins and the range of the mass-adjusted difference over the draws (angular-size strict counts 7/8 in 598 of 600 draws; with log distance, observed SPS 4/8 to 6/8 and both SPS 3/8 to 6/8).

Reference run: input SHA-256s, seed rule, sample facts (including the per-bin attenuation difference), grid histograms and linear-T50 t range, one-cube summary, software versions, and the tie-rule redraw settings.
Reference run: readable summary tables of the sensitivity outputs.
